A.text: Severe mucositis can interrupt cancer therapy, so this statement is correct.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

B.text: Mucositis causes pain and an inability to eat, so it is not painless or mild in this sense.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

C.text: Good oral hygiene lowers microbial load, which may reduce the inflammatory response and the severity of mucositis, so hygiene does matter.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

D.text: Mucositis commonly follows chemotherapy, high-dose head and neck radiation, and stem cell transplantation, so it is not limited to chemotherapy.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

explanation.text: Mucositis appears as redness and ulceration of the mucosa with pain and inability to eat, and severe cases may interrupt cancer therapy.

cites.section: Dental Management of Pediatric Patients Receiving Immunosuppressive › Oral care during immunosuppression periods and radiation therapy

explanation.text: It commonly results from several therapies, and good hygiene may lessen its severity.
